high.title: [AMD's Latest AI Chips Attack Market — New GPU and CPU Products on 2nm Process, TSMC Plays Key Role]
high.summary: AMD launched its latest AI chip lineup at the "Advancing AI 2026" event on July 23, unveiling the MI455X GPU and 6th-generation EPYC CPU — both manufactured on TSMC's (2330) cutting-edge 2nm process. These two chips together form AMD's "Helios" rack-level solution. The MI455X is designed for frontier AI and AI factory deployment, featuring HBM4 memory and delivering up to 34x higher token throughput and up to 18x lower token cost compared to the previous generation. Industry observers are bullish that as AMD's new AI chips begin shipping in volume, TSMC's advanced node order pipeline will remain robust and continue to heat up. While Nvidia still dominates the GPU market, AMD's aggressive push signals intensifying competition ahead. **Market implications:** This is directly positive for TSMC's advanced node utilization and revenue visibility. Investors in TSMC should view this as incremental demand confirmation, with the 2nm node now seeing multi-customer adoption, reducing concentration risk and supporting long-term wafer pricing power.

high.title: [Google Raises Capex Guidance — MediaTek, Hon Hai, and Supply Chain Partners to Benefit]
high.summary: Alphabet (Google's parent) raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to USD $195–205 billion, up from the prior guidance of $180–190 billion, surpassing analyst expectations and breaching the $200 billion "red line" some investors had flagged. The revision is driven by surging AI demand, with Google Cloud revenue jumping 82% YoY to $24.77 billion last quarter, and backlog orders reaching $514 billion. Gemini monthly active users hit 950 million, closing in on ChatGPT's ~1 billion. Analysts suggest Alphabet's 2027 capex could exceed $280 billion. Industry observers expect Taiwan's key supply chain partners — including TSMC, MediaTek (2454), Hon Hai, and Quanta — to benefit meaningfully from this sustained hardware investment cycle. **Market implications:** This is a strong positive signal for Taiwan's AI server and semiconductor supply chains. MediaTek and Hon Hai in particular stand to gain from increased chip design wins and server assembly orders respectively. Fund managers should monitor order flow updates from these names in upcoming earnings calls.

high.title: Trump Tariffs Strike Again: Taiwan's Partial Goods Subject to 10% or 12.5% — Effective U.S. Eastern Time July 24
high.summary:
The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) announced on July 23 that it will impose tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on major trading partners — including Taiwan, the EU, Japan, South Korea, and Switzerland — replacing the temporary 10% tariffs that expired at 12:01 AM Eastern Time on July 24. Under Section 301, the new rates are calculated by subtracting the Most Favored Nation (MFN) tariff rate from the applicable 10% or 12.5% rate, with detailed product-level specifics to be published in the Federal Register. Certain exemption categories exist, including goods whose tariffing could cause domestic U.S. supply shortages, products not producible in sufficient quantity domestically, and select Taiwanese goods where exemptions would encourage commitments against forced-labor imports. Steel, aluminum, automobiles, and certain agricultural and energy products are excluded from the new tariffs. **Market Implications:** This development is critically relevant for Taiwan's export-oriented listed companies — particularly technology hardware, electronics, and components manufacturers. Companies such as TSMC, Hon Hai, and MediaTek supply chains may face margin pressure if downstream U.S. customers absorb higher input costs. Fund managers should reassess earnings guidance sensitivity for Taiwan exporters and monitor whether FSC or CBC respond with any FX or liquidity support measures.

high.title: U.S. Currency Report Does Not Label Any Country a Manipulator — Taiwan and 9 Others Remain on Watch List
high.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department released its semi-annual currency report, concluding that no major trading partner manipulated its exchange rate to gain an unfair competitive advantage in 2025. However, Taiwan remains on the Treasury's "Monitoring List" alongside China, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam, Germany, Ireland, and Switzerland — the same 10 economies flagged in the January 2026 report. A country is placed on the watch list if it meets two of three criteria under the 2015 Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act: (1) a significant bilateral trade surplus with the U.S., (2) a large current account surplus, and (3) persistent one-sided foreign exchange intervention. Taiwan's continued presence on the list signals ongoing U.S. scrutiny of the CBC's FX management practices. For fund managers, this is a key risk factor for the New Taiwan Dollar: any perceived aggressive NTD depreciation by the CBC could escalate tensions with Washington, potentially constraining the central bank's policy flexibility. It also adds a layer of geopolitical uncertainty for exporters and life insurers with large USD-denominated foreign asset portfolios.

high.title: Foreign Investors Buy for Second Consecutive Session — Three Key Factors to Watch
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market posted a modest gain of 0.06% on July 23, closing at 44,850 points after volatile intraday swings of 749 points. TSMC (2330) led a late-session recovery, closing up 0.2% at NT$2,405. Critically, all three major institutional investor categories turned net buyers simultaneously for the first time since July 1, with combined net purchases of NT$18.52 billion. Foreign investors were net buyers of NT$6.95 billion — marking a second consecutive session of foreign buying — while also reducing their net short position in TAIEX futures by 1,397 contracts to 75,198 contracts, suggesting a modest easing of bearish hedging. Institutional analysts note the market remains in a consolidation phase between the quarterly and monthly moving averages, with volume contracting 9.2% to NT$930.6 billion. The three key variables to monitor are: (1) U.S. mega-cap tech earnings, (2) Federal Reserve policy direction, and (3) sustained foreign capital flow trends. The concurrent reduction in futures short positions alongside spot buying is a constructive signal worth tracking closely.

medium.title: [Wistron Bullish on AI — Chairman Lin Hsien-ming Says Demand Will Only Keep Growing, Orders Secured for Years Ahead]
medium.summary: Wistron (3231) Chairman Lin Hsien-ming expressed strong confidence in the AI market on July 22, stating that AI demand "will only continue to grow" and drawing parallels with the cloud storage boom, which defied early skepticism to become a sustained expansion. President Lin Chien-hsun added that orders for the next several years are essentially secured and that there is no discussion of an AI bubble within the industry. Wistron plans to expand capacity in Taiwan, the US, and Southeast Asia, with 2027 capex expected to exceed this year's NT$60 billion. The company's first-half revenue surpassed NT$1 trillion, partly attributed to internal AI deployment that effectively doubled operational efficiency. This commentary reinforces the broader AI infrastructure spending narrative and is consistent with signals from major hyperscalers including Google and others.

medium.title: [Tesla's Massive Capex Push — Robots and Self-Driving Focus; Taiwan Supply Chain Links Highlighted]
medium.summary: Tesla reported strong Q2 revenue growth of 26% YoY to $28.24 billion, but profits missed expectations as capital expenditure surged, with free cash flow turning negative for the first time in over two years. CEO Elon Musk guided full-year capex exceeding $25 billion, with spending expected to continue rising over the next two to three years, focused on humanoid robots (Optimus) and autonomous vehicles (Cybercab). Musk also noted that TSMC and Samsung's US fabs will be critical components in these initiatives. Taiwan supply chain beneficiaries flagged by analysts include Asia Optical (3019), Mirle, and Hota. Tesla shares fell over 13% in early US trade on concerns about return timelines, which investors should monitor for potential read-through to Taiwan supplier sentiment.

medium.title: [KKR to Exit Lee Chang Yung (LCY) Stake — Sets Stage for Accelerated Semiconductor Materials Expansion]
medium.summary: LCY Group President Lee Mou-wei confirmed in a Bloomberg interview that private equity firm KKR plans to gradually divest its stake in LCY Chemical, acquired in 2019 for approximately NT$47.8 billion (~USD $1.56 billion). The exit is expected to free LCY to pursue a more aggressive growth strategy in semiconductor materials, with Lee stating he intends to expand "slightly faster than TSMC." US investments in Arizona — projected to come online around 2028 — are expected to scale well beyond original plans, potentially encompassing multiple product lines and partnerships with South Korean and Japanese firms. The identity of potential buyers for KKR's stake has not been disclosed. This is relevant for investors tracking semiconductor materials supply chain consolidation and M&A activity in Taiwan.

medium.title: Taiwan's Financial Three Sectors' China Exposure Approaches NT$800 Billion — Not a Capital Return; Three Key Drivers Revealed
medium.summary:
According to FSC data as of end-May 2026, total China exposure across Taiwan's three financial sectors (banking, securities, insurance) rose to NT$792.4 billion — a nine-month high — up NT$2.85 billion month-on-month, with the year-on-year decline narrowing to 4.3%. However, the FSC and banking industry sources clarify that this uptick is primarily driven by RMB appreciation (up ~3% YTD), stronger A-share valuations boosting mark-to-market asset values, and modest increases in Taiwan-invested enterprise financing needs in China — not a strategic re-engagement with mainland markets. Banking sector exposure accounts for NT$733.06 billion of the total, with the FSC's Banking Bureau Deputy Director noting that the 0.18% monthly increase likely reflects routine client fund flows rather than a shift in risk posture. On a rolling 12-month basis, bank China exposure is still down NT$35.4 billion (-4.6%), with investment positions down 23%. **Relevance:** For fund managers monitoring Taiwan financials and life insurers, this data confirms that the apparent increase in China exposure is an accounting/FX valuation effect rather than a fundamental reallocation, and overall risk appetite toward China remains cautious and stable.

medium.title: New Taiwan Dollar Closes at 32.266, Appreciates by 1.09 Cents
medium.summary: The NTD strengthened by NT$0.109 against the USD on July 23, closing at 32.266 compared to the prior session's close of 32.375. Intraday range was 32.230–32.380, with an opening at 32.340 and total turnover of USD 1.947 billion. The NTD appreciation is notable given the same-day U.S. Treasury watch list report (Article 1), and may partly reflect foreign investor equity inflows. For life insurers with large unhedged USD asset positions, NTD strength represents a translation headwind on overseas investment returns and book value — a recurring sensitivity for the sector.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Close — Up 25 Points to 44,850; TSMC Closes at NT$2,405 (+0.2%)
medium.summary: The TAIEX closed up 25.03 points (+0.05%) at 44,850.81 on July 23, recovering from an intraday low of 44,340.76. Breadth was negative with 640 decliners versus 443 advancers. Among key names: MediaTek (2454) +0.64%, Hon Hai (2317) +2.38%, Delta Electronics (2308) flat, ASE Technology (3711) -1.06%, UMC (2303) -0.35%, and Nanya Technology (2408) -4.37%. Hon Hai's outperformance is worth noting given its AI server exposure, while Nanya's sharp decline reflects continued weakness in legacy DRAM. Sector-wise, computer peripherals (+2.24%) and other electronics (+2.08%) led gains, while semiconductors (-0.06%) and financials (-0.13%) were modest laggards.
